steps.content:
In August of N.F. 115, the combined efforts of multiple forces finally destroyed BR-005. EDGE covertly recovered the suspected Underground inheritance, securing it under maximum custody. With that, the anomalous Tides of Ashes ceased, and the farland forces requested a ceasefire. The specter of war that had loomed for nearly a year finally dissolved.

But EDGE found no peace in victory.

In the wake of the BR-005 crisis, EDGE moved with unsettling speed. Using unknown means, they re-concealed the BR-003 suspended in the sky. Orders flashed to FAC, the 9th Agency, MBCC, and others: intensify sweeps of Black Ring ruins and hunt the suspicious.

They were watching for the Underground, as if it were a terror eclipsing war itself.

Two days later, the hunt yielded its first catch.

Unidentified Mania fluctuations pulsed along the contamination trail of BR-005's migration. A joint operation was immediately launched, tracking the signal to a single, suspicious figure hiding within the blighted zone.

The pursuit proved punishing, not just because of the complex contamination saturating the tear zone...

August 25, N.F. 115
DisCity
WhiteSands
BR-005 Ruins
Bang, bang, bang—BOOM!!

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: Target's broken loose, vector 3 o'clock! O26's in position! We're pushing him that way—thirty meters! Get ready to intercept and—
As the order is still being spoken, the target is already pivoting. He narrowly dodges the paralysis rounds fired from O26's automated turret, then raises his own weapon in reply.

His precise shots—somehow placed through the chaos of gunfire and cover—hit O26's critical systems. The turret shudders and dies. With an easy vault over the disabled machine, he disappears. Beside the monitors, the commander is left slack-jawed.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: ...His anticipation is perfect. Was the op compromised? No. He's read our tech and tactics before we even move. He knows us.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: Outland infiltration? Or a turncoat from inside?
Your eyes flicker across the combat data logs, then the grainy footage from the field. Static washes over the feed, but you lock onto a detail in the enemy's movements.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Those aren't standard rounds, more like some Mania contamination. He's manipulating the ambient contamination in the ruins. Clearing paths, sealing routes. It's too fluid.
—You switch to the Mania scanner.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The signature isn't Sinner-derived... If this reading's right, it's likely some <color=#fb9259>Underground sorcery</color>. But why's his movement pattern...
You don't get to finish. Your own words—certain keywords, already out—have just tripped the security alarm.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: An <color=#fb9259>Undergrounder</color>?! This is bad! The 9th Agency is exposed!

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: All units, listen up! The target could be from the Underground, capable of sorcery-based contamination manipulation! Ambient contamination is his weapon!

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: Non-Mania combat units, do not engage solo! I repeat, do not engage solo! This is extreme risk!

The warning comes a few seconds too late. Across the way, an agent, codenamed <color=#fb9259>Thorn</color> from the 9th Agency, has already abandoned his cover. For years, he's survived the brutal front lines against the Underground. His experience is vast, his resolve unshakable, and it's focused entirely on the present moment.
Surveillance was the assignment, but it no longer matters. He has already chambered a round, his aim steady on the approaching target.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: It's Underground sorcery! "Thorn," fall back!! You're getting yourself killed!!

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Combatant
steps.content: No... That's one of those Underground bastards. I'm not letting him slip through!

Thorn charges out, gun blazing. Rounds strike the suspect squarely in the chest, yet the lethal barrage only tears through the man's outer garment. As the fabric shreds, something tumbles from the suspect's chest pocket, catching Thorn's eye.

It's a thin fragment of red crystal. It slices through the contaminated air as it plummets. One glance is all it takes; Thorn's pupils dilate in shock. He lunges, reaching out, but his fingers close on empty air. The crystal shatters against the ground instantly, lost in the swirling dust and sand.
A brief, profound silence cuts through the chaos of the battle.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Combatant
steps.content: ...That belongs to <color=#fb9259>him</color>. Why do you have it?

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Combatant
steps.content: ...Did you kill him...?

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Combatant
steps.content: Did you kill <color=#fb9259>Rust</color>, you son of a *****?!!

His rage erupts. In a zone this saturated with Mania, such fury is a flashfire to a soldier's reason. Thorn charges in, a reckless blur through the contaminated air, hell-bent on tearing his enemy apart.

The man across from him hesitates for a moment, then holsters his gun and raises his hand. A red mark sears into the palm of his leather glove, and instantly, the surrounding contamination surges to life. Half of it weaves into a net before him, while the other half lashes out like tendrils, coiling around Thorn's protective boots and yanking him off balance. Thorn crashes hard to his knees.
He refuses to yield. Even grounded, he fires shot after wild shot. In that moment, he feels a presence from behind as another figure vaults over him and charges ahead.

steps.speaker: Thorn
steps.content: Chief?!
Your sudden arrival freezes them both. Reacting first, the "Undergrounder" casts a sorcery—not in front, but behind you, catching Thorn's already-committed bullets in a wall of swirling corruption.

That's all the confirmation you need. Your eyes, attuned to Mania's flow, see past the spectacle. None of the "sorcerer's" attacks were meant to connect. They were misdirection. Thorn is untouched. His recklessness has become a trap, and the "Underground sorcerer" is the one who's been cornered.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...The openings are too obvious.

With that thought, you accelerate, aiming yourself like a projectile at the swirling wall of contamination separating you from your target. A heartbeat from impact, it tears open, a perfectly timed exit you fully anticipated.

steps.speaker: Undergrounder?
steps.content: Ugh...

The ruins' own contamination empowers you as well. From two meters out, your shackles lash forward, spearing the murky air to plunge deep into his body. You don't stop moving. Your momentum carries you into him, crashing him to the ground and pinning him down with your full weight.
It's shockingly easy.
He offers no resistance. Once pinned, he just lies there, resigned. He even begins to catch his breath.
Your shackles continue to pulse with agitation, their red glow undimmed. It illuminates half of his face: deathly pale, and smiling.

steps.speaker: Undergrounder?
steps.content: Heh... As brave and reckless as ever.

The voice is unfamiliar. The face, one you have never seen. Yet in an instant, a tremor passes through your shackles—a jolt that stirs fragments of memory buried deep within. They rise to the surface, sharp and achingly familiar.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Who are you?

He offers no answer, only a cryptic smile as his eyes shift to a point just over your shoulder. Your reaction is a fraction of a second late. A blurred figure clears you in a vault, and the hardened stock of a rifle crashes into the captive with brutal force.

steps.speaker: Thorn
steps.content: Let go!
BWAK!
[Black Screen]

The manhunt is a success. The captive is a confirmed Sinner—and one who wields Underground sorcery, no less. This revelation draws considerable attention.
"Thorn," the 9th Agency operative instrumental to the operation, insists on participating in the man's interrogation.

You politely but firmly decline every request.
Before a more rigorous interrogation can begin, there are personal matters you need to confirm with <color=#fb9259>that person</color>. Alone.
When you see him again, his wounds have mostly healed, far faster than any normal person could recover.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: Hello, Chief. You look well, much better than before. It's good to see.

The man sits across from you in the sterile glare of the interrogation room. His unnervingly radiant smile only accentuates the impression of a corpse's grin. You find yourself mentally reviewing the cold facts again:
A face you've never seen. A voice you've never heard. DNA that returns no match in any database, civilian or covert.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: Alright, let's get this over with. What do you want me to explain? BR-005? Mania contamination? Underground sorcery?

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: I hope I haven't caused you too much trouble. Wouldn't want to cut into your downtime.
He's playing the cooperative role. You pick your first question.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: Suspect, spy, Underground madman... pick one. Your colleagues have been very polite about it.
...Heh. You shrug.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: What do people call you? Friends, family, enemies, and what do you call yourself?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I want to know your <color=#fb9259>real name</color>.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: Not everyone has a name, Chief ${PlayerName}. And not everyone has someone who remembers them.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: So call me whatever you like. I'd be honored.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Is that so? Then I'll call you...
The man tilts his head, playing the connoisseur.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: A bit rough around the edges, isn't it? I was hoping for something more dashing.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It came to me as soon as I saw you. I think it fits.

Your gazes lock. Eyes betray more than words ever could; in that silent exchange, mutual assessment is instantaneous. He recognizes you—this much is clear. His demeanor is amicable, yet deliberately reserved. For your part, you make no secret of your probing intent.
The charade ends. You simply hand him a document.

[Personal File: "Rust"]

Classification Level: A

"Rust" was recruited as an informant by 9th Agency operative Thorn in Eastside. Following severe Mania corruption during a support mission in N.F. 106, he was withdrawn from service for intensive treatment.
Operations recommenced in N.F. 107. Under directive from upper management, he was reassigned as a stationed informant in the West District. Primary duties involved monitoring Mania-weapon trafficking within the Inner Bay area and observing suspect activities of Rustfire.

During this tenure, he sustained regular contact with "Thorn". All activities are logged. No anomalies have been identified through subsequent audit cycles.

In N.F. 112, authorization was granted for his involvement in special operations targeting crypts in the West District outskirts. He provided advance warnings of the risks posed by Parma. While only partially implemented, these warnings were later validated. Proactive measures by FAC, informed by his intelligence, contributed to containing the BR-004 crisis. This outcome facilitated the 9th Agency's subsequent negotiations with FAC to secure control of the MBCC.

Post-transfer, operational protocols for "Rust" were substantially eased. He was granted autonomous operational status with direct reporting channels to Intelligence Director Langley Blackett. At his personal request, he continued his post at the Inner Bay Drifter Camp, maintaining solitary surveillance of Rustfire. Though certain intelligence was selectively reported during this phase, he delivered critical, timely briefings on Underground plots and potential locations of Corpus 002, providing material support to the MBCC Chief's anti-Mania operations.

After the Rustfire riot in April, N.F. 113, he was repeatedly tasked to assist EDGE in recovery operations for the missing MBCC Chief. While he supplied the requested intelligence, all search initiatives concluded without success.

In November N.F. 113, preceding the High Tower Black Ring operation, "Rust" declined participation in a scheduled EDGE search operation for the first time. He subsequently ceased all communication. His last recorded position indicated an entry into the active BR-002 contamination zone.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: Hmm... A low-level informant recruited by the 9th Agency. The records are surprisingly thorough. I'm impressed.
He flips to the next page.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: Intelligence operations continued until November of N.F. 113, right around the time the High Tower Black Ring erupted in the West District. Then he went dark...

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: He must be dead by now. Are you grieving for him?
He offers a smile as he slides the documents back across the table to you.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: There's no need for that, Chief. This was the 9th Agency's failing.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: For assets like this, everything is strictly compartmentalized. Even if they die, word wouldn't—and shouldn't—reach your ears.

options: What can I do? I already know.

choices.text: What can I do? I already know.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And I want to know more.

[Death Report: "Rust"]

Classification Level: A

In December of N.F. 113, cleanup operations at the West District High Tower Black Ring ruins reached a temporary conclusion.
Among the recovered remains of former Rustfire insurgents—most killed during BR-002's berserk state—one male corpse, found near the former Black Ring core, was flagged as anomalous.

The body exhibited extreme trauma, originating not from the Black Ring or Corruptors, but from a series of exquisitely precise and brutal Mania sorceries. Forensic analysis identified nearly twenty distinct types, all classified as Underground sorcery, administered by multiple perpetrators.

Evidence confirms the subject endured prolonged torture. The perpetrators deliberately sustained his biological functions to facilitate profound psychological devastation.
Termination occurred only when the High Tower Black Ring began exhibiting anomalous activity, immediately prior to the destruction of BR-002.

A preliminary identification was made by Agent "Thorn" based on a unique Mania-crystalline residue recovered from the remains. Biometric verification confirmed the deceased as the missing operative, "Rust".

All prior charges of defection against "Rust" have been formally rescinded. His operative status is reinstated; his death is registered as an honorable sacrifice.
However, all related data has been sealed under direct orders from the 9th Agency command.

Ring researchers have claimed the remains for study of the inflicted Underground sorceries. "Rust's" operative records have been expunged from active databases. He will rest in silence—as a Rustfire insurgent, another anonymous casualty of the High Tower Black Ring.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: He cared a great deal about his partner. He's never come to terms with it being a cold case. Spent the last two years digging for answers, and for whoever's really responsible.

The man studies the photographs. The remains are mutilated beyond recognition—images so profoundly grotesque that they have, on more than one occasion, overwhelmed even you. His expression, however, remains flawlessly composed. After a moment, he lifts his deathly pale face and turns it toward you.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: ...Then calling me by that name would only make things worse, wouldn't it?

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: That agent, "Thorn," is convinced I killed his partner. That "Rust" died at the hands of an <color=#fb9259>Undergrounder</color>—me.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: To have his comrade's life taken, and then his name stolen by the same person... It will be devastating.
You look at him.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: What Thorn needs is the truth. The truth about what happened to "Rust."

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If you're feeling charitable and don't want to upset him, then tell me everything. I'll pass it along. Might give him some peace.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: You're asking an Undergrounder for the truth?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Corruptors, Puppets, humanoid monsters like Parma... my shackles have touched them all. That sickening sensation is something I will never forget.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But you're nothing like them. You're a <color=#fb9259>Sinner</color>, with a unique constitution that lets you operate inside a Black Ring. It's why my shackles can stay within you.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: Perhaps you simply haven't met enough of my kind.

options: True. I haven't seen nearly as much as you have.

choices.text: True. I haven't seen nearly as much as you have.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But I've never met an Undergrounder who couldn't bear to hurt a human. Even with Thorn's gun in your face, you refused to harm him. You even went out of your way to protect him in secret, right there in the heart of the contamination.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Thorn was convinced that you killed Rust because he recognized something of "Rust's" on you. So I don't see a problem if I draw a different conclusion from the same clue.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: That's a rather... unconventional line of reasoning, Chief. Shouldn't you be presenting me with scientific evidence?
He hands the documents back to you.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: Since you have the autopsy report, you should also have access to "Rust's" biological data from the time of his death. Even better if the 9th Agency still has his physical examination records from recruitment.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: Compare all of it to me as I am now, and you'll find—

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: From a purely biological standpoint, Rust and I are two entirely different individuals. We don't even share a blood relation.
He's not wrong. You don't rush to agree, however. You simply hold his gaze, watching.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: Still not convinced? Then let's discuss something else. An agent of his caliber must have left behind a few connections, wouldn't you say? Informants, friends, enemies... and that partner of his, so eager to avenge him.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: You could always invite them here to identify me in person. Let's see who else—besides you—would ever accept that I've simply... inherited "Rust's" identity.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: Though, if you do go through with it, I'd need your protection. Can't have that partner charging at me again.
Your stare doesn't waver. After a moment, he lets out a weary sigh.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: Alright. It seems you're holding onto other compelling evidence, Chief, to be this certain in your identification.
Looking into his eyes, you start to speak, pace deliberate.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You're right. There are gaps I can't explain. I've never seen his face, never known his whereabouts. When I checked with the 9th Agency, they admitted their star agent preferred to work alone. No one knew the details.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: "Rust" left no trail. So when new questions came up, I had no choice but to ask you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Bullets and rifle butts can't fake a death. Whoever brought me to the Drifter Camp in N.F. 112 must have used some kind of Mania sorcery. And in N.F. 113, while I was out, I was moved around more than once, by his hand. And then there's you...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I know the person in this world who understands "Rust" best isn't Thorn. Isn't Langley. Isn't anyone from Rustfire... It can only be you. As for why, you're going to tell me.
For the first time, the glib, slippery tension that could have sustained your duel indefinitely crystallizes into silence. He looks at you, and his gaze is suddenly a honed edge.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: ...Who told you that?
There it is. The expression you were waiting for.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Then let's trade answers. I mean you no harm, and "Rust" was once a comrade I trusted. If the truth is what I suspect, then honesty helps us both. But the more you dodge and hide, the more you look guilty.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And once my suspicion latches onto someone... it tends to become a headache for them.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: No matter how many times you change your face, your voice, your identity... no matter how well you hide, you won't shake me until I get a satisfying answer.
For a long moment, neither of you moves. Finally, the tension leaves his shoulders, and he leans back.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: Then it seems I have no choice but to tell you everything...

The man holds your gaze as he raises a hand to his collar. He loosens it, then deliberately draws his lapels apart, revealing what has been carefully hidden all along: the base of his neck, his collarbones, his upper chest.

steps.speaker: Haha, writing about the honorable deeds of heroes is a crime in your eyes, huh?

steps.content: Thick, ropy scars cover every inch of his exposed skin. They resemble the marks of Black Ring corruption you've seen on Hella. These, however, are more extensive, and gouged far deeper. What lies beneath them isn't flesh and blood, but a seething, formless chaos. Stare too long, and you feel your own mind straining at the edge, threatening to tumble in.
The man's face shows no pain. He watches you, calm and assessing, as if what he's bared is not a mutilation carved into his own body, but simply bait on a hook.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: Judging by your reaction, you've seen something like this before. This is what happens when a human fuses deeply with a Black Ring, complete with its curse... and its blessing.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: The ability I gained is simple enough: bodies are merely vessels I change at will, and I can always transfer my consciousness through the Black Ring.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: Whenever a body is destroyed beyond repair—when it dies—my consciousness returns to the Black Ring. It waits until the Ring connects to a suitable replacement... Say, when someone is infected with Mania and their mind collapses, but their body has yet to twist into a Corruptor...

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: My drifting consciousness seeps through, claims that hollow, ownerless shell as my own, and is reborn in another body... Sound familiar?

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: Yes, that <color=#fb9259>Parma</color>, the Undergrounder who gave you quite some trouble, used a similar trick. You might ask the 9th Agency how many times they had to kill him before he finally stayed dead.

A sharp, intentional malice emanates from him, and you register every edge of it. Still, you choose stillness over reaction. The urge to discover what fuels his venom outweighs the instinct to avoid it.
He notes your momentary slip and the iron control that instantly corrects it. A smile of genuine approval touches his lips before he yields to your order.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: The "Rust" in your reports is at least the third body I've used. It seems to have belonged to a fallen 9th Agency agent, likely "Thorn's" actual partner when he was alive.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: I grew rather fond of it. Convenient, and it came with a wealth of useful knowledge and skills. When it was destroyed in N.F. 113, I was... genuinely reluctant to let it go.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: Come to think of it... before I claimed that body, could he have been one of those dear <color=#fb9259>Rustfire comrades</color> you still think about?
[Shackles Effect]

You rise, and your shackles lash out on pure instinct, piercing through his body. The sensation is startlingly vivid this time. Through the psychic link, you can feel the wet, tearing resistance of muscle and fascia.
Yet none of that agony reaches the man's face. He is still smiling, the expression welded onto his corpse-pale features, his gaze locked on you without a flicker.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: There we are. You shouldn't be so quick to count me among your own, Chief... My ties to the <color=#fb9259>Underground</color> run far deeper than you realize.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: There's no point in being vague with the timeline. If you were truly using Rust's body, then at the very least, we can confirm one thing: the person killed by the Undergrounders at BR-002 was you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So what exactly do you mean by your "ties" with them? When did you enter Rust's body? What triggered it? Who were you before that, and what have you done since becoming "Rust"?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Don't try to dodge by unsettling me. Answer me. Tell me the truth.
You try to pull your shackles back, to reassert control of the interrogation... but it seems you're already behind.

The luminous barbs of your shackles protrude from wound after wound across his skin. You try to pull them back, but meet a faint, grotesque resistance. It's a sickening tug, like drawing a blade from clotted mire.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: Heh... I've given you quite enough intel. Now, it's your turn to answer a few <color=#fb9259>little questions</color> of mine.

The fissures across his body glow ever brighter, bleeding crimson light. An indescribable presence saturates the room. Suddenly, you can no longer be sure—is this still the interrogation room? Is this reality? The air thickens with something viscous, clogging your senses.
...All you can perceive is the man before you and the chaotic aura shrouding him, growing more vivid, more glaring with each second.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: Who I am now bears no resemblance to "Rust." Before my candid confession, there should have been no clues, no evidence, no one who could have connected me to him... except you.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: So steadfast in your conviction, completely unmoved... Why?

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: Chief... Why are you so certain that I am Rust?

Something is wrong. Your body tenses to leave, to shout a warning, but a turbulent wave of familiarity crashes over you, pressing you back into the seat and guiding your tongue. You grapple with it, fighting the magnetic pull to give him your raw, unguarded truth.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Those who know me would say I can be... confident. Unreasonably so, sometimes.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: Now it's your turn to be evasive? No matter. Just as you seem to have a knack for seeing through me, I'll study you just as closely. I'll uncover everything you wish to hide.

The man offers a polite nod before his gaze drops to the spikes piercing his body. He lifts a hand, his fingers brushing lightly against one of the shackles' barbs. Red light erupts, and a piercing ring floods your ears, instantly silencing the interrogation room's alarm.
Your senses blur into a formless haze. It feels less like an assault and more like a return, to something gentle, known. Like home. Like... a Black Ring. His face tells you he feels it too.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: The shackles... I failed to account for them during the manhunt a few days ago. That's how I ended up in your hands... But now that I think about it, the look on your face when you caught me was rather interesting.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: In that moment, did you see anything through the <color=#fb9259>shackles</color>?
You bite back a verbal response. Yet within, his question finds its mark, provoking an answer that forms against your will.
[Flashback: Chapter 9 Shooting CG, Chapter 10 Chief's Speech CG, Chapter 13 Chief Lying in Coffin CG (solo, without Don)]

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: ...It's come this far already? It seems your shackles have grown considerably since we last met two years ago. You've personally entered and destroyed two Black Rings since then, haven't you?

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: Did you <color=#fb9259>devour</color> them, just like before? BR-005? BR-002? Or did you take them all? Did EDGE not stop you? Or perhaps I should put it this way...

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: After such a feast, how have you changed? Who exactly is ${PlayerName} now? The Chief of Minos, or the <color=#fb9259>shackles of Mania</color>?

His hands suddenly clamp down on the spikes impaling him. A corresponding jolt lurches through your consciousness, followed by a wave of visceral nausea. The Sinner before you distorts, dissolving into a chaotic, humanoid mass that writhes hungrily to devour the shackles themselves.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: Please, tell me the truth. "Rust" received interrogation training. He can spot a lie. Don't try to deceive me.

steps.speaker: Stranger
steps.content: Otherwise, no matter how powerful your shackles may be, I might just do something drastic... and hurt you at any cost.

His grip tightens. The shackles blaze white-hot, burning through his leather gloves, melting the skin of his palms, searing into something deeper—his very essence. It is not only the uncanny Mania that presses down on you with menace, but the raw intensity burning in his eyes.
Holy hell! If I'd known you packed this much firepower, I'd have dragged you everywhere! Just imagine how invincible we'd look together—the invincible EMP with an ace like you!
[Flashback]

steps.speaker: Thorn
steps.content: Chief?!
Yet every time, he held back his attacks. With you, with Thorn—even at the cost of his own advantage.
[Exit Flashback]

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...There's no need for you to worry. Even cautious as they are, EDGE isn't concerned about my shackles. That should tell you they have it under control. And... threatening me won't work. If you could so easily "hurt" someone, you wouldn't have been caught and brought here.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Your actions are far more honest than your words, Mr. Many-Faced Agent. When it comes to you, I'd rather trust my instincts.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And my instincts tell me there's no need to treat you as an enemy, or a prisoner. We didn't have to speak like this.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Tell me about yourself. What you've been through, what you're fighting for, what weighs on you now, and why you keep hiding the truth from us.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If you're not the Agent "Rust" I thought you were, then tell me your real name. I want to hear it from you.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: ...You're not going to use your shackles to see for yourself? You clearly have the power.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The power to pry into someone's secrets? I don't know if I even have that. And even if I did, I wouldn't use it lightly. Besides...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If you really are "Rust," as I hope you are, then you're my friend.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I won't do that to a friend.

The oppressive chaos gripping your shackles dissolves. The uncanny feeling saturating the space evaporates, leaving only the sterile chill of the interrogation room. The Mania alarm has remained unanswered long enough that flustered voices now clamor beyond the door.
...How strange. That confrontation felt like an eternity. Yet snapping back, only seconds have bled away. And the man opposite you—
The violent fissures that scarred his form have subsided. He sits poised, collar neatly adjusted, his gaze steady upon you.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: My apologies, Chief. That was an ill-timed jest. I'm glad to see you haven't changed, still the most dependable <color=#fb9259>friend</color> a Sinner could ask for.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: As for the matter of "Rust"... perhaps we could save that for another time? That little scuffle took more out of me than I'd care to admit. I'm afraid this body of mine is at its limit. Shameful, I know, that even I have my frailties.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: After all, you've already placed your shackles on me. The interrogation can resume whenever you wish.

The commotion beyond the door pulls your attention for a second. When you look back, his expression has reset. The smile is a placid, unreadable mask. The interrogation is over. You draw your shackles back, the movement slow and final.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Before that, I have one last question.

options: You're the Rust I know, right?

choices.text: You're the Rust I know, right?

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: ...Heh. If seeing me reminds you of him, then by all means, use that name.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: It was only ever a spy's temporary codename, but... to be remembered by you, I'm sure that "Rust" would be pleased.
[Door Closes, Black Screen]
It turns out, you never get him back into that room.

That night, an entire surveillance grid goes dark. Not disabled, but utterly and physically destroyed, in perfect synchronicity before a single alarm can sound. The scale of it is impossible, far beyond the Sinner's known methods. The entire Bureau is left reeling.
By the time repairs are complete, his cell is empty. The only recovered footage is a brief clip of him casually walking out the Bureau's front doors. He glances up, finds the camera—
—and turns to wave you goodbye.
